items.name: MutableBuffer
items.summary: A [`MutableBuffer`] is a wrapper over memory regions, used to build [`Buffer`]s out of items or slices of items.

methods.name: as_mut_ptr
methods.summary: Returns a mutable raw pointer to this buffer's internal memory This pointer is guaranteed to be aligned along cache-lines.

methods.name: as_ptr
methods.summary: Returns a raw pointer to this buffer's internal memory This pointer is guaranteed to be aligned along cache-lines.

methods.name: as_slice
methods.summary: Returns the data stored in this buffer as a slice.

methods.name: as_slice_mut
methods.summary: Returns the data stored in this buffer as a mutable slice.

methods.name: capacity
methods.summary: Returns the total capacity in this buffer, in bytes.

methods.name: claim
methods.summary: Register this [`MutableBuffer`] with the provided [`MemoryPool`]

methods.name: clear
methods.summary: Clear all existing data from this buffer.

methods.name: collect_bool
methods.signature: fn collect_bool<F: FnMut(usize) -> bool>(len: usize, f: F) -> Self
methods.summary: Invokes `f` with values `0..len` collecting the boolean results into a new `MutableBuffer`

methods.name: extend
methods.signature: fn extend<T: IntoIterator<Item = A>>(&mut self, iter: T)

methods.name: extend_bool_trusted_len
methods.signature: unsafe fn extend_bool_trusted_len<I: Iterator<Item = bool>>(&mut self, iter: I, offset: usize)
methods.summary: Extends this buffer with boolean values.

methods.name: extend_from_slice
methods.summary: Extends this buffer from a slice of items that can be represented in bytes, increasing its capacity if needed. # Example ``` # use arrow_buffer::buffer::MutableBuffer; let mut buffer = MutableBuffer::new(0); buffer.extend_from_slice(&[2u32…

methods.name: extend_zeros
methods.summary: Extends the buffer by `additional` bytes equal to `0u8`, incrementing its capacity if needed.

methods.name: from_iter
methods.signature: fn from_iter<I>(iter: I) -> Self where I: IntoIterator<Item = bool>

methods.name: from_len_zeroed
methods.summary: Allocates a new [MutableBuffer] with `len` and capacity to be at least `len` where all bytes are guaranteed to be `0u8`. # Example ``` # use arrow_buffer::buffer::{Buffer, MutableBuffer}; let mut buffer = MutableBuffer::from_len_zeroed(127…

methods.name: from_trusted_len_iter
methods.signature: unsafe fn from_trusted_len_iter<T: ArrowNativeType, I: Iterator<Item = T>>(iterator: I) -> Self
methods.summary: Creates a [`MutableBuffer`] from an [`Iterator`] with a trusted (upper) length. Prefer this to `collect` whenever possible, as it is faster ~60% faster. # Example ``` # use arrow_buffer::buffer::MutableBuffer; let v = vec![1u32]; let iter…

methods.name: from_trusted_len_iter_bool
methods.signature: unsafe fn from_trusted_len_iter_bool<I: Iterator<Item = bool>>(iterator: I) -> Self
methods.summary: Creates a [`MutableBuffer`] from a boolean [`Iterator`] with a trusted (upper) length. # use arrow_buffer::buffer::MutableBuffer; # Example ``` # use arrow_buffer::buffer::MutableBuffer; let v = vec![false, true, false]; let iter = v.iter(…

methods.name: is_empty
methods.summary: Returns whether this buffer is empty or not.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the length (the number of bytes written) in this buffer. The invariant `buffer.len() <= buffer.capacity()` is always upheld.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Allocate a new [MutableBuffer] with initial capacity to be at least `capacity`.

methods.name: new_null
methods.summary: creates a new [MutableBuffer] with capacity and length capable of holding `len` bits. This is useful to create a buffer for packed bitmaps.

methods.name: push
methods.signature: fn push<T: ToByteSlice>(&mut self, item: T)
methods.summary: Extends the buffer with a new item, increasing its capacity if needed. # Example ``` # use arrow_buffer::buffer::MutableBuffer; let mut buffer = MutableBuffer::new(0); buffer.push(256u32); assert_eq!(buffer.len(), 4) // u32 has 4 bytes ```

methods.name: push_unchecked
methods.signature: unsafe fn push_unchecked<T: ToByteSlice>(&mut self, item: T)
methods.summary: Extends the buffer with a new item, without checking for sufficient capacity # Safety Caller must ensure that the capacity()-len()>=`size_of<T>`()

methods.name: repeat_slice_n_times
methods.signature: fn repeat_slice_n_times<T: ArrowNativeType>(&mut self, slice_to_repeat: &[T], repeat_count: usize)
methods.summary: Adding to this mutable buffer `slice_to_repeat` repeated `repeat_count` times.

methods.name: reserve
methods.summary: Ensures that this buffer has at least `self.len + additional` bytes. This re-allocates iff `self.len + additional > capacity`. # Example ``` # use arrow_buffer::buffer::{Buffer, MutableBuffer}; let mut buffer = MutableBuffer::new(0); buffe…

methods.name: resize
methods.signature: fn resize(&mut self, new_len: usize, value: u8)
methods.summary: Resizes the buffer, either truncating its contents (with no change in capacity), or growing it (potentially reallocating it) and writing `value` in the newly available bytes. # Example ``` # use arrow_buffer::buffer::{Buffer, MutableBuffer…

methods.name: set_len
methods.signature: unsafe fn set_len(&mut self, len: usize)
methods.summary: # Safety The caller must ensure that the buffer was properly initialized up to `len`.

methods.name: set_null_bits
methods.signature: fn set_null_bits(&mut self, start: usize, count: usize)
methods.summary: Ensure that `count` bytes from `start` contain zero bits

methods.name: shrink_to_fit
methods.summary: Shrinks the capacity of the buffer as much as possible. The new capacity will aligned to the nearest 64 bit alignment.

methods.name: truncate
methods.summary: Truncates this buffer to `len` bytes

methods.name: try_from_trusted_len_iter
methods.signature: unsafe fn try_from_trusted_len_iter<E, T: ArrowNativeType, I: Iterator<Item = Result<T, E>>>(iterator: I) -> Result<Self, E>
methods.summary: Creates a [`MutableBuffer`] from an [`Iterator`] with a trusted (upper) length or errors if any of the items of the iterator is an error. Prefer this to `collect` whenever possible, as it is faster ~60% faster.

methods.name: typed_data
methods.summary: View buffer as a immutable slice of a specific type.

methods.name: typed_data_mut
methods.summary: View this buffer as a mutable slice of a specific type.

methods.name: with_bitset
methods.signature: fn with_bitset(self, end: usize, val: bool) -> Self
methods.summary: Set the bits in the range of `[0, end)` to 0 (if `val` is false), or 1 (if `val` is true). Also extend the length of this buffer to be `end`.

methods.name: with_capacity
methods.summary: Allocate a new [MutableBuffer] with initial capacity to be at least `capacity`.
